paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
caption: Comparison of massive activations and attention sink phenomena across different gating configurations. Row 1 (Baseline): Significant massive activations and attention sinks emerge after the 6th layer. Row 2 (SDPA Gating): Reduced activations and no attention sinks observed. Row 3 (Value Layer Gating): Similar activations to Row 2 but with residual attention sinks. Rows 4–5 (Reduced Sparsity via cross-head share and NS-sigmoid): Massive activations and attention sinks resemble the baseline.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The figure illustrates the changes in the first token attention score across different layers. The x-axis is labeled "layer" and ranges from 0 to 20, with a linear scale and uniform intervals of 5. The y-axis is labeled "first token attention score" and spans from 0.0 to 1.0, also with a linear scale and uniform intervals of 0.2. There are two lines on the graph: a blue line representing the "first token attention score" and a green dashed line indicating the mean score of 0.481. The blue line starts at a low value near 0.07 at layer 0, remains relatively stable until layer 3, and then sharply increases to around 0.6 at layer 5. It fluctuates between approximately 0.4 and 0.7 from layer 6 to layer 18, with a notable peak of about 0.85 at layer 19, followed by a decline to roughly 0.55 at layer 21 and a final drop to around 0.2 at layer 24. The green dashed line remains constant at 0.481 across all layers.

model_annotations.German: This diagram illustrates the first token attention scores across various layers for the "atten_output_gate_wo_sparsity" configuration. The x-axis represents the layer number, ranging from 0 to 23 with intervals of 5, while the y-axis denotes the first token attention score, spanning from 0.0 to 1.0 with intervals of 0.2. Two lines are plotted: a blue solid line representing the first token attention score and a green dashed line indicating the mean score of 0.481. The blue line starts at approximately 0.07 at layer 0, remains relatively stable until layer 3, then sharply increases to around 0.58 at layer 5, followed by fluctuations, peaking at 0.86 at layer 19, and finally drops to 0.21 at layer 23. Notable values include 0.64 at layer 6, 0.52 at layer 11, 0.62 at layer 18, and 0.52 at layer 21.
